title: 2009 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: For what value of \(n\) is \[ \begin{aligned} &i + 2i^2 + 3i^3 + \cdots + ni^n \\ &= 48 + 49i? \end{aligned} \] Note: here \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\)

solutions.text:
For \(k\) a multiple of \(4,\) \[ \begin{aligned} &(k + 1)i^{k+1} + (k + 2)i^{k+2} \\ &\quad {}+ (k + 3)i^{k+3} + (k + 4)i^{k+4} \\ &= (k + 1)i - (k + 2) \\ &\quad {}- (k + 3)i + (k + 4) \\ &= 2 - 2i. \end{aligned} \]

Summing the first \(96\) terms (that is \(24\) blocks) gives \(24(2 - 2i) = 48 - 48i.\)

Adding the next term \(97i^{97} = 97i\) yields \(48 - 48i + 97i = 48 + 49i.\) So \(n = 97.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Group the terms in blocks of four consecutive powers of \(i\)
Each block \((k + 1)i^{k+1} + \cdots + (k + 4)i^{k+4}\) with \(k\) a multiple of \(4\) equals \(2 - 2i\)
